subject: Synaptic Labs — Preflight traffic census & sizing checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@synaptic-labs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Synaptic Labs — Preflight traffic census & sizing checklist

Taylor —

Thanks for the demo today — great conversation. To make sure we size Dedicated correctly and put together a deterministic Reserved Capacity proposal, can you send the following telemetry / answers? We typically use these to produce a near-term fleet plan and burst profile: 

1) Sample traffic extract (CSV) covering a representative 7-day window with these columns: timestamp, route, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, user_id (hashed), success/error flag, latency_ms. If you can include a small KV-cache key for session flows that would be ideal.
2) Expected p95 and p99 latency SLOs for interactive endpoints.
3) Typical prompt mix: percent transactional (short prompts, <64 tokens), percent contextual (200–2048 tokens), percent embeddings/batch.
4) Estimated concurrent active sessions at peak (and whether sessions are long-lived or ephemeral).
5) Any planned burst events (weekly batch jobs, marketing campaigns) with expected QPS and duration.
6) Security/compliance constraints that affect quantization or telemetry retention (e.g., cannot export raw tokens).

If you prefer, we can run a short instrumentation pass on a staging endpoint for ~48 hours and collect a sanitized sample instead.

I copied Marissa and Ben — they'll own the sizing workbook and cost estimate. If you can drop the CSV and any docs to the Drive link below we can turn around a draft within 48 hours.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-synaptic-preflight

Thanks — talk soon.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@synaptic-labs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Huang <alex.huang@synaptic-labs.com>, Procurement <procurement@synaptic-labs.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Synaptic Labs — Preflight traffic census & sizing checklist

Jordan —

Thanks — appreciate the recap. Attached is a 7-day sample extract (synaptic_kv_telemetry_sample.csv). A few clarifications inline: 

- p95 target for user-facing chat is 300ms, p99 700ms. We can tolerate short tail increases during known marketing bursts.
- Prompt mix (approx): transactional 42%, contextual 48% (avg prompt ~650 tokens), embeddings/batch 10%.
- Peak concurrent active sessions last week observed: ~1,200 (ephemeral sessions, average duration ~35s), but we expect a 2–3x uplift during launch in Q3.
- Burst events: monthly billing-run that hits a batch pipeline for ~6 minutes at ~12k QPS (embedding-heavy), plus two product launch spikes (expected 3x baseline for 15–30 minutes).
- Compliance: cannot export raw prompts containing PII; we've redacted text in the CSV. KV keys are hashed.

I placed the CSV in the Drive folder and copied Procurement for contract cadence. Let me know if you need a larger window.

Thanks —
Taylor Reed
Head of Platform Engineering | Synaptic Labs
Attachments: synaptic_kv_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 2.3MB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Synaptic Labs — Preflight traffic census & sizing checklist

Forwarding Taylor's input — good baseline. A few immediate notes for the sizing workbook: 

- With avg prompt ~650 tokens and response unknown, assume symmetric response tokens of ~700 for initial sizing (we can refine once we sample response_tokens column).
- Ephemeral sessions + 1,200 observed peak maps to session-concurrency based pooling; we'll model session affinity for chat and separate batch/embedding pools.
- Monthly 12k QPS embedding batch for 6 minutes: that needs transient burst capacity or a dedicated batch pool. We'll calculate both a reserved steady-state and a burst reserve.

Action items for us: 
1) Jordan — confirm whether Synaptic can share response_tokens distribution; if not, we'll infer from prompt->response ratio observed across similar deals.
2) Ben — please run the sizing workbook with: conservative, expected, optimistic lanes (80%, 200%, 300% of observed peak) and include GPU SKU mixes (A800x, H100-96GB fractional, and quantized 8-bit variants).
3) Karthik — flag any infra constraints for session-affinity (pinning) and note fallback routing options (hosted fallback to a lower-SLA model).

I'll assemble a draft workbook (redwood_preflight_sizing_workbook.xlsx) and drop it to the Drive with the three lanes. Expect a first cut by EOD 1/13.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@synaptic-labs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-13T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Synaptic Labs — Preflight traffic census & sizing checklist

Taylor — quick follow-up: could you share the response_tokens column or a histogram? That will materially change the GPU occupancy estimate for the chat pool. If there's any retention policy that prevents us from seeing raw numbers, a small anonymized histogram (token buckets) works fine.

Also, two clarifying Qs from Procurement we got offline: 
- Are there preferred regions for data residency (we default to us-west for the draft)?
- Any blocking compliance controls for quantized model variants (Synaptic said some models must stay at float32).

If you can ping Procurement and Alex with those items we'll incorporate it into the workbook. We'll also model a burst reserve that can be turned on for the monthly batch job.

Thanks —
Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@synaptic-labs.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-15T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood sizing workbook (first cut) — Synaptic Labs

Taylor / Alex —

Attached is the first cut sizing workbook: redwood_preflight_sizing_workbook.xlsx. Highlights in the 'Executive Summary' tab: 
- Three lanes modeled: conservative (1.0x), expected (1.8x), launch (3.0x).
- Suggested steady-state reserved: 8 A800x equivalents (slotting for session-affinity), with an H100-96GB pool for high-throughput batch / embeddings.
- Burst reserve: additional 12 A800x-equivalent capacity for 30-minute windows to cover launch spikes and monthly batch if run on-demand.
- Estimated monthly token cost delta across lanes and quantization savings (8-bit) shown; note model restrictions will increase cost if float-only enforced.

Next steps: 
1) Taylor — confirm response_tokens distribution or grant a 48-hour staging pass to capture an aggregated histogram.
2) Alex / Procurement — if region/us-west is OK we can seed a Reserved proposal and term sheet; otherwise tell us your preferred region.
3) We'll prepare a draft reserved capacity contract with SLA tiers and an optional burst pool addon.

Attached: redwood_preflight_sizing_workbook.xlsx (Excel, 860KB)

If you prefer a short walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
